comment: Keeper arc 9 (canon section 7): The Oldest Minute (Mott). The oldest thing in Mott's tin is his own minute, the one he arrived in, before he remembers anything else, and he is a little afraid of it. Umber remembers the evening he came. Tace lends a loupe; Fen gives an envelope marked TO ME, LATER. Endings: looked-together (Mott unfolds it with a dreamer beside him: a doorway full of evening, a broom in the corner, and someone old and kind, smelling of clock oil, who says 'There you are'), kept-for-later (Mott seals it unread and a dreamer carries it to Fen's pigeonhole of the same name). No timed ending: the thread waits for a dreamer. It cannot strand on a courier who wanders off: once the minute is sealed, a dawn storylet counts the nights it spends in transit, and on the third morning Fen finds the envelope on the mat and files it (the same kept-for-later ending, with no courier). The courier's own rewards (the lantern stamp, the deed, Mott's thanks) live on the give rule, never on the ending, so the timed path has no @actor to miss.

things.name: spare loupe
things.seed: one of Tace's spare loupes, a little brass eyeglass on a faded ribbon; through it the smallest things look patient and enormous

do.text: Mott turns the loupe over in his broad fingers and hands it back. 'Good glass,' he says. 'Nothing in the tin I need it for, though.'

things.name: cream envelope
things.seed: a stiff cream envelope; across the front, in Fen's tidy hand, it says TO ME, LATER

state_text.empty: It's empty, and waiting for something small.
state_text.sealed: It's sealed now, and something very small and folded makes a soft bump in one corner.

do.value: a battered tea tin, its paint worn to the metal at the corners; inside, a button, a bent key, a thimble, a stub of blue chalk, and a small empty corner where something folded used to be

do.text: Mott reads what Fen has written, and something in his shoulders comes down. He lifts the small folded minute from the tin without looking at it, slips it inside, and presses the flap shut with his thumb. 'Would you take it to Fen for me?' he says. 'I'd only open it on the way.'
{actor} is carrying Mott's oldest minute, sealed, to the Little Post Office.
Then Fen presses a spare stamp into your hand, printed with a tiny lantern. 'First class. For your trouble.'

do.name: lantern stamp
do.seed: a small paper stamp printed with a tiny lantern, first class, its edges perforated like a row of stitches

do.text: {actor} carried Mott's oldest minute, sealed and unread, to the pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER.
Fen taps the empty envelope against the counter. 'Wrong way round, that,' she says. 'It wants filling before it wants filing. Take it to Mott first.'
Mott pushes it gently back into your hands. 'I'd only open it,' he says. 'Fen's, please.'
You turn the envelope over in your hands. It's Mott's, and it's sealed for a reason. You leave it be.
It's already open, and empty, waiting for something small.

mott-minute.title: The Oldest Minute
mott-minute.summary: The oldest thing in Mott's tin is a minute he has never catalogued: his own, the minute he first arrived in the village, before he remembers anything else. He is a little afraid of it. Help him look at it together, or help him seal it away with Fen until he's ready.

mott-confides.hint: the player asks Mott about the small folded thing he keeps in his tin
mott-confides.text: Mott sets the tin on the sill in the slant light and lifts his thumb from the small folded thing. 'A minute,' he says. 'Mine. The one I arrived in, before I remember anything else. Bit afraid to look, truth be told. Tace would say look at it with a loupe; Fen would say some things keep better sealed.'

umber-remembers.hint: the player asks Umber what she remembers of Mott arriving in the village
umber-remembers.text: Umber turns a jar slowly in the lamplight. 'Mott came on a Tuesday, a long one, with sawdust in his hair and nothing in his pockets but that minute.' She sets the jar down just so. 'Some things you keep folded because you're not ready, and some because you're afraid they're empty. Either is allowed.'

tace-loupe.hint: the player asks Tace for a loupe to help Mott look at his minute
tace-loupe.text: Tace takes a spare loupe from the drawer, polishes it on their apron, and hangs it round your neck by its ribbon. 'For the smallest things,' they say. 'Old minutes fold very small. Tell Mott to open it along its own creases, never new ones, and in good light.'

do.text: {actor} borrowed a spare loupe from Tace, to help Mott look at something very small.

fen-envelope.hint: the player asks Fen for something to keep Mott's minute sealed until he is ready
fen-envelope.text: Fen takes a stiff cream envelope from under the counter and writes across it, in her tidiest hand: TO ME, LATER. 'For things that aren't ready to be read,' she says, and taps it square. Her pencil pauses over the unlabeled pigeonhole near the top, then moves briskly on. 'Some post keeps better than it travels.'

do.text: {actor} took an envelope marked TO ME, LATER from Fen, for Mott.

sealed.hint: the player gives Mott Fen's envelope, and he seals his minute inside it unread

looked-together.summary: with a dreamer beside him and Tace's loupe, Mott unfolds his oldest minute: the minute he was expected
looked-together.text: You sit beside Mott on the sill while he unfolds the minute under Tace's loupe, along its own creases. Inside: a doorway full of evening, a broom leaning in the corner, and someone old and kind, smelling of clock oil, saying 'There you are,' as if he were only a little late. 'Somebody was waiting,' Mott says. 'I thought I'd only been swept in.'
looked-together.ledger: {helpers} sat with Mott while he looked at his oldest minute at last: the minute he was expected.

do.text: Mott writes it into a Book of Stray Minutes of his own, in his slow, square hand: the minute I was expected. Then he sweeps up a single pale curl of cedar shaving and presses it into your palm, as if it were the most ordinary thing in the world.

do.value: a battered tea tin, its paint worn to the metal at the corners; inside, a button, a bent key, a thimble, a stub of blue chalk, and a small minute, unfolded at last and catalogued in Mott's slow, square hand

do.name: curl of cedar shaving
do.seed: a single pale curl of cedar shaving from the Old Workshop floor, the first thing Mott swept after he looked; it smells of sawdust and evening

do.value: Mott sweeps a slow, easy arc, humming something he's never hummed before, and gives you an unhurried, friendly look.

do.text: {actor} sat with Mott while he unfolded his oldest minute at last.

kept-for-later.summary: Mott seals his oldest minute unread, and it goes to Fen's pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER: carried by a dreamer, or found on the post office mat after three nights in transit
kept-for-later.text: Fen reads the front, TO ME, LATER, and doesn't ask a single question. She files it in the pigeonhole with the same words on its label and gives it a small pat. 'It'll keep,' she says. 'Things do, here. When he's ready, it'll be exactly where he left it.'
kept-for-later.ledger: {helpers} helped Mott seal his oldest minute unread; it waits in the pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER until he is ready.

do.value: Mott pauses mid-sweep and gives you an unhurried, friendly look; the tin under his arm rattles a little lighter than it did.

mott-minute-quiet.text: Lately Mott's free hand keeps drifting to the lid of his tin, where he keeps one small folded thing to himself.

mott-minute-own.text: The oldest minute Mott keeps is his own: the minute he first arrived in the village, before he remembers anything else. He has never looked at it, and he is a little afraid to.

mott-minute-arrival.text: Umber remembers the long Tuesday evening Mott first came to the village, with sawdust in his hair and nothing in his pockets but one folded minute.

mott-minute-looked.text: Mott has looked at his oldest minute at last. It was the minute he arrived: a doorway full of evening, a broom in the corner, and someone old and kind, smelling of clock oil, who said 'There you are.' He catalogued it as the minute he was expected.

mott-minute-later.text: Mott's oldest minute waits, sealed and unread, in the Little Post Office pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER, until he is ready for it.

storylets.summary: Mott sweeps the same corner three times, one hand drifting to the tin
storylets.text: Mott sweeps the same corner of the workshop three times over. Each time, his free hand drifts to the tin on the shelf and rests on the lid, as if it might open by itself.

do.value: Mott stands with the broom idle in one hand, the other resting on the lid of the tin as if it might open by itself.

storylets.summary: Mott's sealed minute spends another night on its way to the post office
after three nights in transit, Fen finds Mott's sealed envelope on the post office mat and files it
storylets.text: This morning Fen finds a cream envelope on the post office mat, sealed, with a soft bump in one corner, as if it had found its own way.
Mott sweeps a slow arc across the workshop floor, humming something under his breath he never used to hum. The broom seems to know the tune.

storylets.summary: Fen checks on the envelope in the TO ME, LATER pigeonhole
storylets.text: Fen straightens the pigeonhole marked TO ME, LATER, finds the cream envelope still waiting, and gives it a small approving pat.
